tasks.prompt:
okay visually there are too many elements and are way too complicated.. let's start from the lite AI modules. the widgget of "your rule" should be simplistic. I don't need any of the little small gray text underline to explain things. for example, "You asked for this every 1 user turn. This is turn 1" or "logo/icon YOUR RULE" delete such stuff. Also the widgget (like a chek-in rule) is too prominent. i want it more like a card-pop up that can be easily closed with a cross on the top right. the wigget should be concise, and only have height that is shorter than width. fields like "A note to yourself" should be deleted, unless the user really want it - which should be an independent module called "memo", if the user tick that, then yes, they can define a textfield where they write stuff under/on the side that is just a side memo which is not sent to the chat. make it a separate intervention module. 



also, now I want you to expalin to me what is the logic of the customized rules, what are the minimal elements/building blocks?
i'm thinking, on one dimension, we should let the user be able to control the timing of the intervention/rule (when is it delivered? before the start the whole chat? every turn? every several turn? at the end of each turn or before each/several turn? or cross-session?)
the second dimension is ways of delivering the change/intervention: (1) UI, like the memo, or simply a text; (2) the user set a meta prompt to control the conversational behaviors of the chat; (3) maybe something else more fun?! ...

first explain to me your current implementation, think about what I just said, and make proper changes.
tasks.assistantExcerpt:
Updated and pushed. [Open Lite AI](http://127.0.0.1:3000/).

Previously, rules were **context → trigger → action**. They mostly interrupted before an AI reply, and check-ins bundled reflection questions with private notes.

Your proposed separation makes more sense. The minimal building blocks are:

| Block | What it controls |
|---|---|
| **When** | Chat starts, first turn, every turn/every N turns, or on request |
| **What** | Show a card or change conversational behavior |
| **Content** | The question, choices, or instruction |
| **Scope** | Which explicitly selected contexts it applies to |
| **Duration** | One occurrence, one reply, or the whole conversation |

“Before/after” now explicitly means **before/after the AI reply**. A chat-start rule can appear before the first user message.

I made these changes:

- **Smaller, landscape cards:** removed “YOUR RULE,” icons, trigger explanations, reflection fields, and completed-rule rows. **× skips once**; disabling remains in Customize.
- **Independent Memo module:** off by default, enabled by checkbox, with an editable label and side/below placement. Its contents never enter chat, model requests, or exports.
- **Clearer builder:** organized around **When** and **What**, with context tucked away.
- **Conversational instructions:** apply without opening a card. Chat-start instructions last throughout that chat; other triggers affect one reply.

Two limits remain explicit: **cross-session scheduling is not implemented**, and free-text meta-prompts require a live model. The simulation demonstrates selectable brief, question, and step-based replies.

For a more playful delivery family, I’d explore **interaction mechanics**: revealing answers in stages, alternating writing turns, or letting users assign just one part of a task to AI. These can use the same timing system.

Verified with 30 tests, production build, and desktop/mobile checks.

tasks.prompt: can you connect the site for me so that we can continue working?
tasks.assistantExcerpt: Lite AI is running again at [localhost:3000](http://127.0.0.1:3000/), with live updates enabled so we can continue editing.

**“Demo reply shape”** selected the simulator’s canned response: brief text, one question, or short steps. It doesn’t interpret your written instruction yet. I renamed it **“Simulated reply style.”**

**“Context”** was a manual filter. I renamed it **“Apply this rule to”**:
- **Every chat:** always eligible.
- **Writing chats only / Reflection chats only:** eligible when you select that **Chat type** above the conversation.

I also removed **“Request a check-in”** and **“On request”** timing completely. Existing on-request rules retain their content but are disabled until you choose automatic timing.

Pushed to the repository. All 31 tests and the production build pass.
